reason: Section 15.3 is a multi-part heritage property phase-in regime with definitions, eligibility approval, formula rules, notification duties, finality, section-application rules, and an offence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Heritage property definitions and approval criteria
proposedGroups.reason: The opening provisions define the heritage-property terms and establish the Minister and Director approval pathway.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the heritage property terms and approval criteria for heritage assessment phase-in.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the phased assessment percentages, base year, eligible floor area, and effective duration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the heritage property phase-in amount, base year, floor-area percentage, and duration are determined.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections impose notification duties when credits, eligibility, or criteria change.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must notify the Minister or Director when heritage property credit eligibility or criteria change.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Heritage finality, section-application rules, and offence
proposedGroups.reason: The closing provisions state finality, when sections 25, 27, 28 and 37 do or do not apply, and the notification offence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the finality, section-application, and offence rules for heritage property assessment phase-in.

reason: Section 15.31 has distinct definitions, application and approval rules, a three-year assessment formula, continuing duties and duration, and finality, section-application, or offence provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Multiunit residential building application and approval
proposedGroups.reason: The first three subsections define the building and base year and state when and how an application is approved.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may apply for multiunit residential building phase-in and what criteria the Director applies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Multiunit residential assessment amount and duration
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions set the three-year percentages, base year determination, effective duration, and bar on duplicate applications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the three-year multiunit residential assessment phase-in and when an approval takes effect or ends.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ongoing criteria, finality, section-application limits, and offence
proposedGroups.reason: The remaining provisions impose continuing compliance and notice duties, make Director decisions final, preserve review of assessment amounts through named sections, and create an offence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the continuing duties, finality rules, section-application limits, and offence for multiunit residential building phase-in.

reason: Section 15.4 sets separate temporary formulas for 2011 and 2012 eligible residential property, each with its own transfer exception.

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the 2012 assessment formula and transfer exception for eligible residential property.

reason: Section 15.5 combines a current-year definition and eligibility rule with two alternative formula values, a minimum amount, and transfer exceptions across several years.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Eligible residential assessment formula for listed years
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections define current year, identify eligible residential property, and set the lesser-of-J-and-K formula with a minimum value.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the eligible residential property formula framework for 2013-2017, 2019, and 2020.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transfer exceptions for eligible residential property
proposedGroups.reason: The last two subsections state how transfers in 2012 or in a current year displace the formula.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when transferred eligible residential property is assessed at real and true value instead of under section 15.5 formulas.

reason: Section 15.6 carries forward 2017 assessment amounts for 2018, identifies Director-determined exemptions, and requires a modified 2018 notice.

reason: Section 15.7 is one formula regime for eligible residential property from 2021 to 2024, including the K calculation, minimum value, and transfer exception.
